WIZ_PROJECT_ID.description: Wiz project id (UUID) whose Issues should be imported. Scopes the IssuesTable GraphQL query (filterBy.project=[<id>]) so the import only walks the requested project's findings; resolves the project metadata for the host description from the matching nodes[].projects entry in the response.

WIZ_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (info | low | medium | high | critical). Forwarded to Wiz as filterBy.severity (so the tenant only paginates results that survive the floor) AND enforced client-side after Faraday severity normalisation (handles Wiz's CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/INFORMATIONAL enum and CVSS base-score fallback). Defaults to info (no filtering).

WIZ_STATUS.description: Optional Wiz issue status filter (CSV of OPEN | IN_PROGRESS | RESOLVED | REJECTED). Forwarded to Wiz as filterBy.status. Defaults to all statuses (no filter). REOPENED is normalised to OPEN. Whitespace and case-insensitive.

name: wiz
title: Wiz (CNAPP)
description: Wiz Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) GraphQL importer. Pulls cloud-security issues from a Wiz tenant via the canonical POST /graphql IssuesTable query and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. The IssuesTable query enumerates issuesV2 (paginated via first / after cursor) with filters on status / severity / project; each node carries id / severity / status / sourceRule (Control or CloudConfigurationRule) / projects / entitySnapshot (the affected cloud resource) / createdAt / updatedAt / dueAt / resolvedAt / statusChangedAt / notes / serviceTickets. Each Wiz project becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because CNAPP findings live on cloud resources, not on IPs) with hostnames = {projectName}@{projectId}; per-project issues attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per issue id with [CNAPP] engine prefix, '{ruleName} on {nativeType} {resourceName} [{region}]' in the title, rule description / rule_id / resource / cloudPlatform / providerId / region / subscription / resourceGroup / externalId / issue status / severity / createdAt / updatedAt / dueAt / resolvedAt / statusChangedAt / projects / notes in the description; sourceRule.resolutionRecommendation / remediationInstructions / remediation / recommendation / solution surfaces as Faraday resolution. Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed, deduped across issue + rule), Wiz-Rule: pivot label, entitySnapshot.cloudProviderURL, serviceTickets[].url and serviceTickets[].externalId. CVE list harvested from rule.name / rule.id / id / title (CVE-shaped token fallback) + cve / cveId / cve_id / cves / aliases (string + list-of-string + list-of-dict shapes, deduped case-insensitively across both issue and rule). Severity normalised from Wiz's string enum (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW / INFORMATIONAL — also accepts Important / Major / Moderate / Minor / Informational / Information / Negligible / Trivial / None / Unspecified / Unknown) with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric score is surfaced (≤0/>10 → info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); WIZ_MIN_SEVERITY both forwarded to Wiz as filterBy.severity AND enforced client-side after normalisation. Status mapped from issue.status (OPEN / IN_PROGRESS / REOPENED → open, RESOLVED / FIXED / CLOSED → closed, REJECTED / IGNORED / WONT_FIX / RISK_ACCEPTED / SUPPRESSED / MUTED / FALSE_POSITIVE → risk-accepted). Auth: Wiz exclusively uses OAuth2 client_credentials. A service account is created in the Wiz UI, the client id / secret are stored in WIZ_CLIENT_ID / WIZ_CLIENT_SECRET, and the auth tenant URL is WIZ_AUTH_HOST (e.g. https://auth.app.wiz.io). The API tenant URL is WIZ_HOST (e.g. https://api.us4.app.wiz.io — the region segment varies). The audience defaults to wiz-api but is overridable via WIZ_AUDIENCE for tenants that mint scope-narrowed tokens. The token exchange is POST {WIZ_AUTH_HOST}/oauth/token with form body grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=...&client_secret=...&audience=... and returns {access_token, expires_in, token_type}; subsequent GraphQL calls send Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
